previous_assumption: Granting `equipment.manage` to the "owner" role (via the Stage 5 seed migration) was sufficient to restrict Machine management to Rental Company organizations, since only a Rental Company's owner was expected to exercise it.
correction: Roles (owner/member) and role_permissions are global, not scoped by organization type — every organization's owner, Renter included, ends up with `equipment.manage`, since organization type never entered the permission model. Confirmed live: a signed-up Renter organization's owner could create and list Machines via the API, and the frontend Sidebar showed "Equipment" in nav for Renter accounts too. Fixed by adding a domain-rule check (`EquipmentService.requireRentalCompanyOrganization`, using a new `OrganizationRepositoryPort.findWithTypeById`) that 403s equipment operations for any non-`rental_company` organization regardless of permission — this is a business invariant ("Renters don't own fleet"), not something `equipment.manage` alone can express, so it lives as an explicit check in the service, not a permission split. Mirrored client-side via `NavItem.requiredOrganizationType` so the nav link itself doesn't appear for Renters. Rule of thumb for future domains (Rental, RFQ): whenever a capability is meant for only one organization type, do not assume the permission grant alone enforces that — check organization type explicitly, since roles/permissions in this schema are not organization-type-scoped.
